verdict.rationale: First-party docs say the moq-relay server can be self-hosted, including forming a self-hosted CDN cluster. The docs also say users can host their own CDN, and the setup demo starts a relay locally. A community production report (SageOx) shows clients publishing to a relay that fans out to their own subscribers, which corroborates real-world operation. missing for 10: detailed deployment and operations documentation in the pack, and explicit independent confirmation that the report's relay was self-operated rather than hosted.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: [moq-relay](/bin/relay/) - A server connecting publishers to subscribers, able to form a [self-hosted CDN cluster](/bin/relay/cluster.html).
Host your own CDN, use a 3rd party service, and/or connect P2P via Iroh (native only).
You can optionally self-host a private CDN or end-to-end encrypt your content.
The default demo starts a relay, publishes a test video, and opens the web player.
